source_text.body:
Set up news alerts with a browser agent
Testers had Operator set up news alerts and save a summary; it followed a logical path but was slow and Google blocked login, so they leaned toward cancelling.
Done with
OP
Operator
What they did
The testers asked ChatGPT to write a detailed prompt for their AI News Scout and gave it to Operator. It created alerts, but workflows stalled and needed manual fixes. They restarted with a simpler prompt asking for a daily table of the top 10 consumer-AI articles, emailed through ProtonMail. Operator found the news slowly, and the email login needed hands-on help.
How it went
The second attempt worked better, but the emailed report was badly formatted and hard to fix. Rerunning a saved task repeated the whole flow. They called it not worth it yet and leaned toward cancelling.
Worth knowing
Operator needs the $200/month Pro plan. Google blocks logins from its virtual browser, so use something like ProtonMail, and automatic sending needs an integration such as Zapier.
Try it yourself
with
Operator
Copy prompt
Set up news alerts for [topic or company] using [alert service, e.g. Google Alerts] with [frequency]. Then save a short summary of the alerts you created and their settings in [place to save]. Before submitting any sign-in or subscription form, pause and show me what you are about to do. If a login is blocked, stop and tell me.
Original source: https://consumeraidecoded.substack.com/p/building-an-agent-with-operator
